subject: Hosted API latency SLO: window synchronization & stability fallback policy
messages:

Cc: HorizonPay Ops <ops@horizonpay.com>
Date: Mon, 03 Aug 2026 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Hosted API latency targets and measurement windows

Hi Mina,

Thanks again for the demo last week — HorizonPay is excited about Redwood's latency profile. Before we push the pilot live, legal is asking for clarity on the p50/p95 commitments and how you measure them across regions. Two asks from our side: 

1) Can Redwood commit to a synchronized p50/p95 across US regions (we're trying to avoid region-to-region drift)?
2) We need a documented measurement window and carveouts for maintenance and controlled bursting. HorizonPay's SREs want to understand how short-lived bursts are handled (e.g., 5–30 minute spikes).

High level target we had in mind for hosted API during pilot: p50 <= 75ms, p95 <= 500ms. We can be flexible if you propose a stability/fallback policy that includes canarying and crediting for prolonged degradations.

I've attached a short list of questions from our Ops and Legal teams (questions_from_horizonpay.docx). Can you propose a single-page operational commitment + fallback policy we can use in the amendment?

Best,
Elena Ruiz
Director of Platform Engineering
HorizonPay

Attachments: questions_from_horizonpay.docx (docx, 18KB)

From: Mina Haddad <mina@redwood.com>

Cc: HorizonPay Ops <ops@horizonpay.com>
Date: Mon, 03 Aug 2026 13:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Hosted API latency targets and measurement windows

Hi Elena — thanks for the clear asks and the questions doc.

Short answer: yes, we can offer a synchronized measurement approach and a provisional fallback policy for the pilot. Below is a concise proposal you can circulate to Legal/Ops. If acceptable, we'll convert it into an amendment and attach an evidence package for the monitoring period.

Provisional operational commitment (pilot):
- Measurement basis: rolling 14-day window by default, aggregated at the account-region pair and then synchronized across US regions for contractual evidence.
- Targets: p50 <= 75ms, p95 <= 500ms for the synchronized US footprint during the pilot.
- Burst handling: automatic transient carveout for spikes shorter than 15 minutes per-minute granularity; repeated bursts where >5% of minutes in a 24-hour period exceed p95 will be considered sustained and count toward the window.
- Canary & stabilization: new deployments or model swaps trigger a 7-day canary measurement excluded from contract penalties but included for observability.
- Fallback policy: automatic routing to compensated-compatible model variant (same quality class, lower GPU footprint) when a region exceeds sustained thresholds; if fallback does not restore p95 within 60 minutes, customer is eligible for service credits capped at 2% of monthly hosting fees for the affected account-region.

Next steps:
1) If HorizonPay agrees in principle, we'll send a one-page PDF (provisional-sla-offer.pdf) and an evidence bundle template (slo-evidence-metrics.csv) you can use to verify during the pilot.
2) We recommend a 90-day pilot window with 14-day rolling measurement for the first 30 days and then a move to the standard 30-day rolling window if both sides are satisfied.

I'll loop in our sales lead and product for approval; copying them now.

Thanks,
Mina Haddad
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
mina@redwood.com

Attachments: provisional-sla-offer.pdf (pdf, 72KB); slo-evidence-metrics.csv (csv, 12KB)
